text: RWB-P1-DM001-APP is the rework that replaces the withdrawn migration, not a migration: it builds the account and arrears read path over v_ace_account, v_ace_bucket_log, v_ace_product and v_ace_branch keyed by account_key at the ACE business date, plus the per-service Flyway version that creates nothing for account or arrears rows and records the removal in its history row. It keeps the legacy title 'Migrate account and arrears' and the two legacy test case IDs TC-DM-001-01 and TC-DM-001-04, and it copies no legacy AC text because AC1 to AC3 are withdrawn.
why: The Work Package keeps one APP slice for the legacy key while D-RCV-35 (U1) removed the migration and withdrew its criteria and tests, and the slice would otherwise have no deliverable.
read: Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3, RWB-DM-001 rows Status, Decision, Why, Read path instead, Data product, Withdrawn IDs and Later home; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-06.md; Template and Rules v1 §R5.2, §R6 and §R7
confirm: Data steward and the recovery tech lead at the wave 4 entry check
impact: The story can be built and tested as written; a later correction of the title changes the title line and the file name only, not the story key or the legacy key.

text: The account and arrears read path is read as the four Section A views keyed by account_key at the ACE business date, with the answer shaped by the P1 read contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP and the field order taken from the field IDs DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042, DF-ACE-140 to DF-ACE-145, DF-ACE-146 to DF-ACE-150 and DF-ACE-151 to DF-ACE-154, the bucket history newest month first, a missing account answered as not-found with nothing written, and the late batch answered from v_ace_batch_status with the last completed date, the status STALE and MSG-P1-001, reading no parameter and no reference list.
why: The legacy row names the views and the purpose but gives no answer shape, no paging, no not-found behaviour and no per-source cut-off, and this story's pattern set holds neither DP-06 nor DP-07, so no parameter or reference read is available to it.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-001 row 'Read path instead'; FSD P1 v3 A2.3 and A2.14; TSD P1 v3 T3.3, T3.4 and T3.7; Template and Rules v1 §R7.3
confirm: Data architect and the recovery tech lead
impact: The read path, its tests and the migration can be built from Day 1 against the view fixture; if a cut-off parameter is later agreed, one configuration step and one test change are added and no criterion changes.

text: The story is built from Day 1 on RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, the platform Flyway contract, and keeps wave 4 and business epic EP08 as the Work Package fixes them; its read path is released with the wave 1 service deploy, where the P1 read contract and the freshness stamp are live, and the release date stays 30 November 2026, tentative.
why: The Work Package fixes wave 4, EP08 and Day 1 together, while the service is wave 1 and the account read is the source of the wave 1 case screens; no source settles which tag governs the release of the read path.
read: Template and Rules v1 §R5.6, §R5.7, §R4 service table; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 service table and slide 15; FSD P1 v3 A2.18
confirm: Release manager and the recovery tech lead at the wave entry check
impact: The build and the tests start Day 1 and are not gated by a wave; only the deploy window of the read path depends on this reading, and a later ruling moves the deploy without changing the story or its criteria.

text: The account and arrears read is answered behind GET /accounts/{id} on the base /api/recovery/source-data/v1, one hop with a 2 s budget, published by RWB-P1-E1069-APP, with the login rwb_source_data and SELECT on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views; this story adds no path, no operation and no answer field of its own and takes the architecture over the module specification under §R3.
why: Architecture v5 slide 15 names the account operation and slide 29 fixes the login, while TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A holds no account operation and no source gives the answer field names; §R3 ranks the architecture above the technical specification, so the architecture governs.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 1075, 1114 and 2063; TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R4 and §R5.5 DP-13
confirm: Data architect and the recovery tech lead
impact: The read path can be built and tested behind the named operation from Day 1; if the operation or its schema changes, the controller contribution and the contract fake change and no criterion changes.

text: The story asserts the removal rather than naming a legacy migration file: its Flyway version creates no table, column, index or grant for account or arrears rows, its description records that the legacy migration does not ship, the history holds no version whose description names an extract, a transform, a load or a reconciliation of migrated account or arrears rows, and the two legacy test case IDs TC-DM-001-01 and TC-DM-001-04 are kept with new Covers and the full new test in the test case master.
why: No source holds the legacy migration file name, and the withdrawn test text of AC1 to AC3 and TC-DM-001-01 to TC-DM-001-04 is not in the masters this run reads, so the story can prove the absence only through the history it writes itself.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-001 row Withdrawn IDs; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.10; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-06.md tcs_legacy
confirm: Tech lead and the QA lead
impact: The removal is testable without inventing a file name, and the two legacy IDs stay traceable; the master's next version records the withdrawal.

text: The story uses three role codes, RW-DATASTEW, RW-TRIBE and RW-COE, as the sources give them, and adds no role that no source holds; RW-CUSTSERV is not used.
why: The Work Package names four roles, and RW-CUSTSERV appears in no source read of this legacy key, its module or the rwb-access role list, so using it would invent a role.
read: FSD P1 v3 A2.1.3.3, A2.2.3.3 and A2.11.3.3; TSD P1 v3 T6.1; the technical enabler stories for RW-TRIBE; legacy RWB-DM-001
confirm: Business analyst and the rwb-access role owner
impact: The authority table names roles that exist as rwb-access rows; adding a role later is one row in rwb-access and one line in §10, with no change to the criteria.
